solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perfect location, you heard, the best: central Siam

indicators.note: heard means we take the sound of the word you, not its spelling
central asks for only the middle letters of the word that follows

blocks.note: the letter U is pronounced like the word you
the top is the best of anything
the two middle letters of Siam

explanation.surface: Someone praises Thailand's capital region as the ideal spot to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is an imagined ideal society, a place where everything is flawless.

clue.text: Charge to restrict right on-line nuisance

indicators.note: restricting something means hemming it in, so one word goes around another

blocks.note: a toll is a charge for using a road or bridge
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A fee imposed to curb some proper behaviour on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside TOLL, after its first two letters, to make TROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll is someone who posts deliberately provocative messages online to upset other users.

clue.text: Specious excuse before phone message

blocks.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
a text is a message sent by mobile phone

explanation.surface: Someone makes a flimsy excuse ahead of sending a message from their phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretext is a false reason given to hide the real one, which is a specious excuse.

clue.text: Copy, ample, regularly used

indicators.note: regularly used means only letters at even intervals are taken, skipping the rest

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of ample

explanation.surface: An instruction to make plenty of copies, used again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic or imitate them, so it is a verb synonym for copy.

clue.text: Area under water in southeast a British journalist follows

blocks.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast
taken as written
B is a common abbreviation for British
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter trails a Briton through some flooded part of southeast England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' just confirms the order: the journalist comes after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The seabed is the ground at the bottom of the sea, a region lying beneath water.

clue.text: Being this, exercise needs a try?

definitions.text: Being this, exercise needs a try?

indicators.note: to exercise something is to work it about, so these letters are put through their paces into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A couch potato is told it's time to give working out a go.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: someone who sits around all day should try exercise; 'exercise' also serves as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentary describes a life of sitting with little physical activity, exactly what exercise would cure.

clue.text: Corner fish

blocks.note: first meaning: a corner, the point where two lines meet
second meaning: to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Someone is told to trap a fish so it cannot escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a command, 'Corner fish' sounds like trapping one; in fact it is two separate meanings side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is a corner formed by two meeting lines, and to angle is to go fishing with a hook.

clue.text: Mistake translating "maturer"

indicators.note: translating turns a word into another form, so its letters are converted into a different arrangement

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A translator has slipped up in rendering the word maturer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratum is Latin for an error, used especially for a printing or writing slip.

clue.text: Field officer referring to boss's facial feature

blocks.note: FO is the military abbreviation for Field Officer
re means concerning or with reference to
the head is the boss of an organisation

explanation.surface: An army officer remarks on something about their commander's face.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after boss stands for has, joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The forehead is the part of the face above the eyebrows, a feature of anyone's face.

clue.text: Talk about king's clothing

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the second

blocks.note: gab is chatter or idle talk
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: People gossip about what the monarch is wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: R sits inside GAB, between its A and B. The 's after king stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for clothes, especially distinctive dress or costume.

clue.text: The Spanish finally comb the river

indicators.note: finally asks for just the last letter of each word it governs

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
last letter of comb
last letter of the second the

explanation.surface: Spanish searchers at last scour the river thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' covers both 'comb' and 'the', taking the last letter of each.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elbe is a major river of central Europe flowing through Germany to the North Sea.

clue.text: Ceremony at first, then often it's thrown

definitions.text: Ceremony at first, then often it's thrown

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word before
letters that are thrown get scattered and land in a new order

blocks.note: first letter of ceremony
the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: At a wedding ceremony, once it's over, something is usually thrown.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: after a ceremony, this is often what gets thrown over the couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Confetti is the small pieces of coloured paper guests throw over a newly married couple.

clue.text: Unexpected rain — cover predator?

indicators.note: something unexpected comes out differently from the norm, so these letters arrive in a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sudden downpour leaves someone wondering whether to take shelter from a hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnivore is a meat-eating animal, and many such animals hunt prey as predators.

clue.text: All actors in show alternatively star

blocks.note: the cast is the full set of actors in a production
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Every performer in the production could be the leading name instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' looks like the lead actor of the show, but it is a real star in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor is one of the two bright stars of the constellation Gemini, the Twins.

clue.text: Assert time is typical

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone claims that time follows a normal pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Average describes what is ordinary or usual, the standard case, which is what typical means.

clue.text: Season of gold corporation needs starting out

indicators.note: starting out points to the very beginning, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, a tum
first letter of needs

explanation.surface: A golden season of business, which a company needs to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' wants to be a company; it is a humorous old word for a large stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumn is the season between summer and winter, called fall in North America.

clue.text: Extremely testy on phone, mostly about old storm

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its first and last letters
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
about means around, so the shortened word surrounds the next piece

blocks.note: outer letters of testy
taken as written before shortening
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone gets very irritable on a call about weather that was mostly in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: PHONE loses its E, then O goes inside the remaining PHON between O and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A typhoon is a tropical cyclone, a violent storm of the western Pacific.

clue.text: Itchy, let loose in bad-tempered way

indicators.note: letters let loose are freed from their order and can scatter into a new one

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An itchy person, once freed, lashes out in a grumpy manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy means irritable and touchy, so tetchily is the adverb for acting crossly.

clue.text: Part of facade thrills trainee

indicators.note: part of says the solution is a piece lying inside the words that follow

blocks.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: An architecture student is excited by a section of a building's front.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training for the armed forces or police, a trainee officer.

clue.text: Small piece of land in place associated with Old Testament

blocks.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
OT is the standard abbreviation for Old Testament

explanation.surface: A little patch of ground in a spot with biblical links.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a small measured area of ground, such as a building plot or allotment.

clue.text: Completed on time? That's clear

blocks.note: something over is finished
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a job was finished punctually and is told it plainly was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the first piece before the second in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly and plainly visible, the opposite of covert, so clear fits.

clue.text: Praise twofold on way back

indicators.note: going on the way back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word reads right to left

blocks.note: dual means double or twofold

explanation.surface: Someone receives double compliments on the return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is to praise highly, a slightly formal synonym used in phrases like lauded hero.

clue.text: One watching rook, lone, confused

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up, so they need sorting into a different order

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A spectator is baffled by a solitary bird, or by a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker is a bystander who observes events without taking part.

clue.text: Circuit of China recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: china means mate in Cockney rhyming slang, from china plate, so a pal

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a tour around China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap is one complete circuit of a racetrack or course.

clue.text: Resolute golfer's support for furniture item

blocks.note: set means determined, as in set on doing something
a tee is the peg that holds up a golf ball

explanation.surface: A determined golfer's backing is used to prop up some furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a long upholstered seat for more than one person, a sofa.

clue.text: Party decoration Dad's welcoming home — cheers after

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
in means at home
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: Father invites someone in and thanks follow at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: IN goes inside PA, and TA follows; the 's after Dad stands for is. Cheers is also British for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A piñata is a decorated container filled with sweets that children break open at parties.
